December financials approved unanimously with operating reserves at $94,200. Seven continuing trash-can-storage violations from the December community sweep move to formal notice. Reserve funding discussion deferred to February.
raw_transcript:
James Crawford: Alright, 7:02, January meeting called to order. Marcus, roll?
Marcus Williams: James, Margaret, David, Sandra, Linda, and myself present. Quorum confirmed.
James Crawford: Sandra, reserve study.
Sandra Chen: Sterling delivered final on the 27th. Headline: $180K funding gap over 10 years. Clubhouse roof moved up to 2028 from 2031, pool resurfacing 2027.
David Patel: Why did the roof move up three years?
Sandra Chen: Storm damage from September accelerated wear. Warranty depreciation gives us maybe 40 percent coverage. I pushed back twice. They're firm.
Margaret Holloway: Motion to accept the reserve study and come back next month to discuss funding options.
David Patel: Second.
James Crawford: All in favor? Five-zero. December financials.
Sandra Chen: Reserves at 94,200. Three percent under landscaping budget, slightly over on utilities. Nothing alarming.
Marcus Williams: Motion to approve.
Linda Garcia: Second.
James Crawford: Five-zero. Violations.

Margaret Holloway: Hold his, send the other six.
Marcus Williams: Revised motion: 6 notices excluding 218 Oak pending medical hardship review.

ai_summary: After a contentious discussion, the board awarded the 2025 landscaping contract to Verde Garden Co over incumbent Greenleaf in a 3-2 vote, citing better irrigation expertise and a $350/month savings. Resident Brenda Olsen raised drainage concerns at the Brookhaven cul-de-sac. The board denied a fence-height ARC request that exceeded declaration limits. February financials approved unanimously.
raw_transcript:
Margaret Holloway: 7:00, meeting called to order. Brenda Olsen present — we'll get to your item in open comment. Sandra, financials.
Sandra Chen: February closed at 89,400 operating after a $2,400 pool house plumbing repair. Within budget.
David Patel: Second. Five-zero. Big item: landscaping contract.
David Patel: Greenleaf's three-year contract expires March 31. Two real proposals: Greenleaf at $5,200/month renewal, Verde at $4,850. Both include weekly mowing, biweekly bed maintenance, quarterly fertilization, irrigation service.
Linda Garcia: Greenleaf has been with us seven years.
David Patel: Their work is fine. But they fumbled zone 4 twice and response time on November storm cleanup was a week. Verde's irrigation lead is a certified backflow tech which Greenleaf doesn't have on staff.
Sandra Chen: $350/month is $4,200/year. Over three years, real money.
Linda Garcia: Switching has costs too. Knowledge transfer.
David Patel: Verde has a 30-day onboarding period included.
Margaret Holloway: I'm inclined toward Verde. The irrigation expertise alone is worth it given reserves told us about system age.
Linda Garcia: I'd give Greenleaf one more year. We have history.
Marcus Williams: Motion to award Verde at $4,850, 12-month term.
David Patel: Second. Three-two. Linda and Marcus opposed.
Margaret Holloway: David, notify both vendors this week.
David Patel: By Friday.
David Patel: ARC fence at 1206 Brookhaven. They want 6 feet, declaration caps at 4 on street-facing sides. Corner lot means two sides are street-facing.
Marcus Williams: Motion to deny.
Linda Garcia: Second. Five-zero.
Margaret Holloway: Brenda?
Brenda Olsen: The Brookhaven cul-de-sac floods every rain over an inch. Drain may be clogged or undersized. Reported twice through the portal, no response.
Margaret Holloway: I apologize, Brenda. I'll respond in writing by Tuesday and get someone out there.

Sandra Chen: So moved.
Marcus Williams: Second. 8:22 PM.

raw_transcript:

Sandra Chen: April operating at $86,100. Pool prep expenses starting — furniture delivery, AquaSafe deposit. All on schedule. Motion to approve.

Margaret will follow up with the attorney on stronger enforcement mechanisms.
raw_transcript:
Margaret Holloway: 7:00. Heavy agenda. Welcome candidates and Mr. Vance, Ms. Mathers. Board election first since it affects who votes on the rest. Patricia Sanderson withdrew Monday for family reasons. Antonio Ruiz, three minutes.
Margaret Holloway: Robert?
Robert Kim: Eight years in Creek Valley. Commercial property management background. Board could use someone who reads contracts for a living. No platform, just want to help.
Linda Garcia: Both candidates strong. Robert's contracts background is a gap on the current board.
Marcus Williams: Motion to elect Robert Kim.
Linda Garcia: Second. Five-zero. Robert, come up.
Margaret Holloway: Hearing now. Ms. Mathers presents, Mr. Vance responds, board deliberates.
Karen Mathers: Mr. Vance lives at 1834 Stonebridge. Since November he has had a rotating group of guests — different cars, different people, almost every weekend. Airbnb listing right there, three-night minimum, $285 a night. 14 separate guest groups documented since November.
Theodore Vance: Family member with health issues in Buford, I'm there a lot, house sits empty. Started renting to friends of friends. Declaration is from 1998. Short-term rental wasn't a concept. I think the restriction is unreasonable.
Margaret Holloway: Reasonableness isn't before us tonight. Only whether you're in violation. Are you renting for periods less than 30 days?
Theodore Vance: Yes.
Robert Kim: How many nights total since November?
Theodore Vance: Maybe 60.
Linda Garcia: Mr. Vance, would you take down the listing tonight if asked?
Theodore Vance: I'd rather discuss a variance.
Margaret Holloway: We don't grant variances at hearings. Deliberation now. Both parties may stay or leave.
Margaret Holloway: Propose finding violation and standard short-term fine. $500 plus $100/day continuing.
Linda Garcia: I'll vote for the finding. $100/day is harsh. Reduce to $50.
Sandra Chen: Continuing fine is what stops the behavior. Without it he pays $500 once and keeps earning $285 a night.
David Patel: Per the matrix it's $100. Don't want to set a precedent of negotiating off the matrix at hearings.
Marcus Williams: Motion as Margaret stated.
Robert Kim: Second. Four-one. Linda opposed.
Sandra Chen: May financials $84,200 operating. All on plan. Motion to approve.
David Patel: Second. Six-zero.
Marcus Williams: Motion to adjourn. Linda second. 9:04 PM.

ai_summary: Emergency meeting to ratify the $9,400 clubhouse HVAC replacement after the system failed June 28 during a heat advisory. Reliable HVAC selected from three rapid bids. Funding from operating reserves; Sandra dissented on the funding source, preferring special assessment discussion. A $1,500 independent mechanical audit was authorized.
raw_transcript:
Margaret Holloway: 7:00. Special meeting for emergency expenditure ratification. Robert, your first emergency.
Robert Kim: Trial by fire. Literally.
David Patel: June 28 around 2 PM during the heat advisory, the clubhouse HVAC compressor failed. Inside temp got to 94 before we shut it down. Three rentals refunded — $750 lost revenue.
David Patel: Reliable HVAC came out Saturday morning. Compressor seized, coil corrosion, 17 years old. Repair $3,800 with no warranty. New unit installed by July 5 was $9,400. Lennox commercial, 10-year parts and labor warranty.
Robert Kim: Three quotes?
David Patel: Reliable $9,400, ABC Mechanical $11,200 four weeks out, Atlanta Climate $10,100 two weeks out. Reliable could start Tuesday.
Marcus Williams: Motion to ratify emergency expenditure of $9,400.
Linda Garcia: Second. Six-zero.
Sandra Chen: Funding source. I think we should treat this as candidate for special assessment. $9,400 across 135 is $70 per home. Operating reserve will drop below $80K, below policy floor of $85K.
Margaret Holloway: Special assessments require 30-day notice and owner vote. We've already paid. We can replenish from 2026 dues. Special assessment in July, two months after violation hearings and three months before annual budget, is bad politics.
Sandra Chen: I'm not running for office. Protecting reserves.
Robert Kim: Voluntary contribution line on next year's invoice as soft middle ground?
Margaret Holloway: 2026 idea, not now.
Marcus Williams: Motion to draw $9,400 from operating reserve with replenishment from 2026 dues.
David Patel: Second. Five-one. Sandra opposed.
Margaret Holloway: Sandra's dissent is in the record.
Margaret Holloway: 17-year-old HVAC failing isn't a surprise in hindsight but no one flagged it as imminent. Want an independent mechanical audit. Robert, you've done these.
Robert Kim: $1,500 covers comprehensive walkthrough — HVAC, plumbing, electrical panel, water heaters, kitchen equipment. Three quotes by month-end.
Marcus Williams: Motion to authorize up to $1,500.
Linda Garcia: Second. Six-zero.
Sandra Chen: June at $82,900 before HVAC hits. Otherwise on plan. Motion to approve.
Marcus Williams: Second. Six-zero.
Margaret Holloway: Marcus, community notice this week — plain language, no panic.
Marcus Williams: By Saturday. Motion to adjourn.
Robert Kim: So moved. David second. 8:15 PM.

ai_summary: Back-to-school traffic was the dominant issue. Speed bumps (~$14K estimated) declined in favor of a $2,400 traffic study. Sentinel Engineering won the mechanical audit at $1,375. Linda will engage Riverbend High parent council. Sandra began 2026 budget drafting.
raw_transcript:
Margaret Holloway: 7:01. Robert filled out the audit RFQ. Sentinel Engineering lowest at $1,375, references checked.
Robert Kim: Did the Wickham subdivision last year. Detailed report.
Marcus Williams: Motion to award Sentinel. David second. Six-zero.
Linda Garcia: 42 signatures asking for speed bumps on Creek Valley Drive. Riverbend High parents cutting through to bypass Highway 41 light. People doing 40 in a 25.
David Patel: Drove it Monday morning. Cut-through traffic yes, but didn't see anyone over 30.
Linda Garcia: Worse around 7:40.
Robert Kim: Speed bumps priced — proper engineered ones $1,800–$2,200 each installed. Four bumps is $7,200–$8,800, more like $14,000 with engineering and permitting.
Sandra Chen: We don't have $14K for this.
Margaret Holloway: County may not permit them — private roads connect to county at both ends.
Linda Garcia: So what do I tell petitioners?
David Patel: Traffic study first. Real data. If 40 mph the county supports intervention. If 32 we look hysterical.
Robert Kim: Cobb Traffic Engineering: $2,400 for a one-week study including first week of school.

Linda Garcia: I'd prefer cheaper interventions — signs, painted lines, speed feedback sign.
David Patel: Those can be part of the study recommendation.

Marcus Williams: Second. Six-zero.
Margaret Holloway: Drainage — county inspector July 30 confirmed drain is theirs and upstream pipe partially collapsed. Ticketed for repair within fiscal year. Means by next July.

Margaret Holloway: 7:00. October annual budget meeting notice goes out this week per the 30-day rule. Marcus, on it?
Marcus Williams: Going out tomorrow. Required content all there.
Robert Kim: Sentinel walkthrough August 26. New HVAC correctly sized and installed — good news. Water heater original to 2008 clubhouse build, currently leaking, replace within 18 months — $4,200. Electrical panel at 70% capacity, no headroom. Plumbing supply lines under kitchen are galvanized at end of life, re-pipe in 3 years, $6,800. Structure sound.
Sandra Chen: New line items: $11K in next 3 years, $4,200 within 18 months.

Margaret Holloway: Motion to accept the Sentinel report.

David Patel: I want to be at 70.

Marcus Williams: Motion to authorize Sterling to formalize revised study at $87,500 and 2027.

ai_summary: The board approved the 2026 budget of $487,400 (5-1) and a 4.8% dues increase to $299/month (5-1, Linda opposed). Reserve funding increases to $94,200 to address revised clubhouse roof timeline and Sentinel audit findings. Marcus voted no on the budget citing communication concerns. raw_transcript:
Margaret Holloway: 7:00. This is the 2026 annual budget meeting, called per declaration with 30-day notice provided September 11. Quorum confirmed. Sandra, walk us through.
Sandra Chen: v3 in your packet. Total operating $487,400. Major lines: landscaping $58,200, pool $24,800, utilities $41,000, insurance $38,500, management $42,000, reserves $94,200, contingency $18,000. Revenue from 4.8% dues plus assessment income covers it with $3,200 buffer.
Robert Kim: Reserve contribution up from $78K to $94.2K. $16,200 more.
Sandra Chen: Drives us to 70% funded by 2027.
Linda Garcia: Want to spend more time on dues. 4.8%. We have retirees on fixed Social Security. I'd like 3% and stretch reserve target out a year.
Sandra Chen: Modeled 3%. We don't hit 70% funded until 2029. Anything fails between — HVAC, storm — we're in special assessment territory.
David Patel: I'd rather pay $14 a month than get a $1,200 special assessment.
Linda Garcia: Assumes failure.
Robert Kim: Actuarial reading of a 17-year-old subdivision is we're entering heavy capex window.
Linda Garcia: Hendersons, Pattersons, Murphys.
Margaret Holloway: Couple the increase with a documented hardship process? David, draft by November meeting?
David Patel: Yes.
Marcus Williams: I want to raise communication. We're sending 135 households a 4.8% increase notice. They don't know HVAC, reserves, audit. One email isn't enough. In-person session.
Linda Garcia: I'll host them. November.
Marcus Williams: Then I'm comfortable on budget. Want it on record 4.8% needs over-communication.
Robert Kim: Motion to approve 2026 budget at $487,400.
David Patel: Second. Five-one. Marcus voted no for the communication record.
Robert Kim: Motion to approve 4.8% dues increase to $299 effective January 1.
David Patel: Second. Five-one. Linda opposed.
Robert Kim: Motion to fund reserves at $94,200.
Sandra Chen: Second. Six-zero.
